record.paper_title: Quo Vadis Strangeness? Strangeness — Open Questions
record.context_brief: Modeling reaction dynamics and nonequilibrium effects
record.original_question: How should theoretical models of flavor observables in relativistic nuclear collisions combine microscopic reaction mechanisms with statistical or kinetic descriptions so that they correctly handle collision dynamics, the transition from quantum to classical dynamics, non-equilibrium effects, and possible novel reaction mechanisms that have not yet been discovered?

evidence.quote: Why do we need so many different models? Nobody doubts that microscopic models are superior to statistical models (and hence is this what we all should be doing?), but some of us also realize that, in practice, microscopic approaches suffer critically from the need to understand and be able to model all relevant and accessible reaction mechanisms, including the novel phenomena that are yet to be discovered.

In fact, even if we had much greater computing power available allowing us to compute within fundamental theoretical approaches such as lattice-QCD [24], we would not know how to treat the dynamics of the collision, the transition from quantum to classical dynamics, the non-equilibrium aspects and many other issues.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad programmatic challenge in heavy-ion theory rather than a sharply defined mathematical conjecture. Hybrid microscopic+hydrodynamic/transport frameworks (e.g., UrQMD+hydro, JETSCAPE, hybrid Boltzmann/hydrodynamic codes) have made substantial progress, but a fully consistent treatment of quantum-to-classical transition and non-equilibrium effects in relativistic nuclear collisions remains an active research area with no definitive resolution.

status_evidence.title: JETSCAPE framework
status_evidence.snippet: A modular framework integrating multi-stage descriptions of heavy-ion collisions combining microscopic and hydrodynamic stages.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art hybrid frameworks combine microscopic and statistical/kinetic descriptions but the unification challenge remains open.

status_evidence.title: Hybrid approaches to heavy-ion collisions (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews of hybrid hydro+transport approaches indicate continuing open issues in non-equilibrium dynamics and quantum-to-classical transition.
status_evidence.claim: Non-equilibrium and quantum-to-classical aspects continue to be unresolved in current modeling.
